narrative.overview: SalesPulse is built for a small business owner with zero technical background, so the system reads like a single well-made instrument rather than a marketing site: one flat surface, one accent color, no chrome that has to be learned. It borrows its restraint from Linear and Stripe's calmer surfaces, not their marketing pages: neutral grounds, a single confident accent, and generous, deliberate whitespace instead of cards-with-shadows everywhere. The one indulgence is the brand mark itself, a small pulse-line glyph that ties the product name ("Pulse") to the literal shape of a sales trend line - now realized in the dashboard's own revenue-trend chart.
keyCharacteristics: Flat by default: borders and tint fills carry state, not drop shadows - KPI cards and chart cards included.

One decorative accent (deep emerald) used identically everywhere in UI chrome; charts with more than one series use a separate validated categorical palette, never the brand accent stretched across series.
System font stack only, no webfont loading, so the app stays fully functional offline.
Two-tier UI-chrome corner radius (buttons/cards) plus one documented exception: chart marks follow the dataviz skill's fixed 4px mark spec.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Pulse Emerald is the only brand color for UI chrome. It never competes with a second decorative hue there; when a second color appears (error red), it signals a real state, not a stylistic choice. Multi-series charts are the one functional exception - see Chart Colors.

rules.name: The No-Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: No uppercase tracked label ever sits above a heading, including chart-card titles. The heading carries its own weight.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces never lift on shadow. If a future component needs to show elevation, prefer a tint or border-weight change before reaching for box-shadow.

dos: Do keep Pulse Emerald as the only decorative accent across every future screen; reuse it for positive/up indicators.
Do keep all containers flat (border + tint, never box-shadow) - KPI cards and chart cards included.
Do keep the two-tier UI-chrome radius scale (8px buttons/marks, 14px containers); chart marks alone follow the 4px dataviz mark-spec exception.
Do keep typography to the single system font stack; do not introduce a webfont without revisiting the offline constraint in PRODUCT.md.
Do use the documented 4-color categorical palette (blue/orange/aqua/yellow, fixed order) for any future multi-series chart; re-run validate_palette.js before adding a 5th color.
Do pair any WARN-contrast chart color (aqua, yellow) with a visible text label, never color alone.
Do use a full tinted-background fill (Success Bg + Success Border) as the highlight signal for synthesized content like the Insights Panel.
donts: Don't add an eyebrow/kicker label above any section heading, including chart-card titles.
Don't introduce a second decorative UI accent color; reserve red strictly for error/negative-delta states.
Don't use box-shadow for elevation; use border/tint state changes instead.
Don't center hero content vertically in the viewport; keep it anchored near the top with generous but capped padding.
Don't use a donut/pie chart for part-to-whole data; use a stacked bar.
Don't style more than one KPI value as a hero figure - all four stay equally weighted.
Don't use a colored border-left/border-right strip as a card highlight; use a tinted fill instead.
Don't call an external API or LLM for the Insights Panel; keep it rule-based and client-side.
